- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent history mean (e.g., 3–5 days), and sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, increase forecast to align with recent upward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- When sentiment shows strong negative trend (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
- If model forecast is above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in upward bias.
- For sentiment history with alternating positive/negative swings, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment trend, not just price history.
